🚨 BREAKING: The FCC accepts SpaceX's application to acquire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum

Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile all told SpaceX "NO" when it asked to use their networks. SpaceX is building its own:

This deal with Grain Management secures 546 paired licenses covering ~100% of the U.S. population, on 800 MHz low band that penetrates straight through walls and already works with almost every smartphone.

Once it closes, SpaceX will hold up to 89 MHz of spectrum in every market it touches.

Elon Musk: "This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America."

fun test of long-horizon coding and the new /swarm feature in Google @Antigravity.

Builder and critic subagents ran iterative loops across Blender and Three.js - checking their own renders to build a playable 3D game of a pelican biking around our Mountain View campus.

STATE OF THE TECH JOB MARKET IN 2026

Twice a year, I dig into trends in hiring and job openings. This is the fifth report I've done, and the most surprising yet:

1. PMs are winning in the AI era
2. Engineering demand has stalled
3. Design openings are at a record low
4. Every role now requires AI skills
5. Tech jobs are concentrating in the Bay Area
6. Remote roles are at a record low
7. The tech job market is growing fast, but mostly outside of software (gasp!)

Full report here: https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/state-of-the-tech-job-market-late

Again, Fable 5.2 is insanely good at 3D modelling: here, it made its own take of that Lord of the Rings scene.

I let the model build its own engine for the water physics, simulating the river as a shallow-water sheet, then running its own 3D particle simulation (FLIP) at 6cm resolution to make the breaking wave

On the horses: anyone who tried to draw a galloping horse knows how hard it is: I gave the model an open static 3D model, then gave it a classic chronophotography of a gallop to build the rigging and animation from.

I had to correct a few things over a few days of iterating + waiting renderings, but it did well!
